items.title: Digital health transformation in Liberia: a hybrid incremental digital transition framework (HIDTF) for sustainable electronic health record implementation
items.abstract: Liberia, like other fragile post-conflict health systems, still relies mainly on paper patient records, and electronic health record (EHR) initiatives have repeatedly failed to reach routine use or national scale. The literature documents the barriers but explains less well why they persist. This conceptual paper proposes three candidate mechanisms and a phased framework, the Hybrid Incremental Digital Transition Framework (HIDTF), for the transition from paper to interoperable EHRs in Liberia. Conceptual synthesis and framework development. Peer-reviewed and grey literature on Liberia and comparable low- and middle-income settings was identified through purposive, iterative searching (PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar) and synthesised narratively by a single author. The corpus is illustrative, not comprehensive, and no quality appraisal or independent screening was done. Constructs from established implementation science frameworks, sociotechnical systems theory and resilience theory, with a political economy lens, were used to derive mechanisms and design requirements. Additional file 1 lists all cited sources and codes the support for each element as a documented finding, a source-author interpretation or an inference by the author. Three candidate mechanisms were proposed. Recursive implementation failure: each abandoned attempt may deplete absorptive capacity and deepen scepticism, lowering the odds of the next attempt. Reliability asymmetry: where power and connectivity are unreliable, reversion to paper can be a rational professional response rather than resistance. Incentive misalignment: donor accountability structures can reward deployment outputs over sustained use. HIDTF proposes five phases and readiness gates (a coordination mechanism and an agreed interoperability approach; minimum infrastructure with offline capability; a trained local cadre) to be met before a site or county digitises. Hybrid paper-digital workflows would be governed as a designed arrangement, and domestic financing would be planned from the outset. No durations or numerical targets are proposed, and four testable propositions are stated. HIDTF is a theory-informed proposal built on secondary evidence from Liberia and comparable settings. The evidence on sequencing is mixed, since one cited source recommends concurrent development, and transferability beyond Liberia is a hypothesis. A Liberian initiative chronology, stakeholder consultation and prospective pilot evaluation are needed before adoption. Not applicable.

items.abstract: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the educational field has expanded teaching and learning possibilities, but has also sparked important ethical and philosophical reflections. This study aimed to map and analyze the scientific literature on the ethical dimensions of AI in teaching and learning processes through a systematic literature search. The search was conducted in the Web of Science database, using the descriptors "Artificial Intelligence" AND "ethics" AND "education." Initially, 1,822 articles were identified; after applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 155 documents remained, of which only 9 comprised the final review. The analysis revealed three main themes: ethical dilemmas related to privacy, algorithmic biases, and student autonomy; philosophical discussions about the role of AI in the teacher-student relationship; and teachers' responsibility when mediated by intelligent technologies. It is concluded that, despite the potential of AI to transform pedagogical practices, theoretical and normative gaps still persist that demand greater scientific and political depth, especially in the development of solid ethical frameworks that guide its application in the educational context.

items.title: Distilling the Shape of Uncertainty: What On-Policy Distillation Learns and How to Predict It
items.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly adopted in the post-training of large language models. However, a stronger teacher may fail to improve the student. Prior work attributes this to a lack of new knowledge, but what that knowledge is remains unclear. We show that OPD learns not only \textit{how to branch}, i.e., which candidate tokens to consider, but also \textit{where to branch}, i.e., where to keep reasoning paths open. The existing token-overlap metric captures only the former. We introduce the entropy shape, the sequence of next-token entropies, to characterize the latter, and propose the Entropy Shape Correlation (ESC) to measure student-teacher agreement in entropy shape. Tracking ESC throughout training and intervening on a teacher's entropy while preserving its token preferences, we empirically show that \textit{where to branch} causally drives OPD gains, independently of \textit{how to branch}. Finally, we formulate OPD outcome prediction as a teacher selection task and establish an evaluation protocol for it, under which pre-OPD ESC selects the best teacher for both students and outperforms existing predictors. Code is available at https://github.com/maybenotime/opd-esc.

items.title: Divergent user expectations of conversational AI: a comparative sentiment and thematic analysis of ChatGPT and Replika app store reviews
items.abstract: Abstract Conversational AI apps are increasingly serving two different purposes: instrumental productivity and emotional support. Although both are built on the same underlying language technology, users may evaluate these systems according to different instrumental and relational expectations. This study examines the differences in user evaluation of a task-oriented assistant (ChatGPT) and a companionship-oriented agent (Replika) through computational analysis of the sentiment scoring, NRC emotion analysis, topic modelling, and inferential tests of the 6,000 publicly available app store reviews (3,000 per application). The two applications differed only marginally in overall review polarity, and the direction of the difference depended on the method used: under the Bing lexicon Replika reviews scored slightly higher (M = 0.312 vs. 0.275), whereas under sentimentr ChatGPT scored higher (M = 0.135 vs. 0.102); aggregate polarity was therefore not a robust point of difference between the two corpora. The rating distributions differed significantly between the applications (χ² (4, N = 6,000) = 242.26, p < .001, Cramér’s V = 0.20), with ChatGPT ratings more polarised at both ends of the scale (36.8% vs. 21.7% five-star; 27.4% vs. 23.8% one-star) and Replika ratings more concentrated in the intermediate categories. Once scores were normalised for review length, Replika reviews contained more joy-, anger-, surprise-, and anticipation-associated language, with all effect sizes small; fear-, sadness-, and trust-associated language did not differ significantly between the applications. The coupling between review language and star rating was weaker for the companion application, though the difference was small (App × Rating interaction, partial η² = 0.016); because the two samples span different publication periods, this interaction is reported as provisional. Topic modelling yielded a six-topic solution in which conversation and companionship accounted for 53.6% of Replika reviews against 10.9% of ChatGPT reviews, while task assistance and usefulness accounted for 30.9% of ChatGPT reviews against 1.2% of Replika reviews. Together, the findings are consistent with differences in evaluative framing between the two applications examined in this study, illustrating two representative cases rather than establishing distinct categories of conversational AI systems.

items.title: Do Preferred and Trusted Attention Cues Support Better Visual Search Performance?
items.abstract: As automated aids become more integrated into daily life and safety-critical tasks, understanding how preference and trust relate to performance becomes important. Automated aids can vary in design, and users may prefer or trust some implementations more than others, even when those subjective judgments do not align with objective performance. In the current study, participants completed a visual search task in virtual reality using different types of cues to search for objects. After the search task, participants responded to questions assessing their preference for and trust in the cue designs. Participants performed better with their most preferred cue than they did on average across the remaining cues, whereas participants did not reliably perform better with their most trusted cue. These findings show that preference and trust provide distinct information about cue designs and highlight the importance of considering both subjective endorsement and objective performance when designing attention cues.

items.abstract: Wang, Lawrence K. 王抗曝 (2026). Dragon² (龖): From Mahjong's "Double Dragon Embrace" to Peaceful U.S.–China Coexistence and Peace Under Heaven -- A Life-Writing Narrative 《龖(Dragon²): 从麻将「双龙抱」到中美和平共存与天下太平的生命书写》. Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics. Lenox Institute Press, MA, USA. 8(10M), 43 pages. (Simplified Chinese Version); ABSTRACT: 本文延续作者对「囍—𩺰—龖」的文化思考,将古字「龖」重新诠释为 Dragon²(亦写作 Dragon2)。囍象征新婚之喜,𩺰象征夫妻无论顺境逆境皆相伴一生;龖则将关怀由家庭延伸至世界。在本文所采用的麻将规则中,「双龙抱」指由两对相同顺子构成的组合,共含四副顺子,每对中的两副顺子花色与数序相同。作者借其「抱而不斗」的意象,将两龙比喻为具有全球影响力的中国与美国,寄托两国相互尊重、和平共存的愿望。这是作者提出的跨文化和平隐喻,并非将龙视为美国固有的国家象征。作者于龙年出生于中国,1949年迁至台湾,后赴美求学、成家与工作。中国承载其出生、文化与早年记忆,台湾见证其成长与求学,美国则承载其深造、事业与家庭生活。这段跨越海峡与太平洋的生命历程,使中美关系成为与自身及家人命运相连的切身议题。本文比较「双龙争珠」「双龙戏珠」「双龙抱」与「双龙护珠」的意象:若明珠代表霸权,两龙可能陷入零和竞争;若明珠代表地球,两龙便肩负共同守护的责任。文章进一步借用工程系统中的回馈、稳定与失控概念,阐述核战无真正赢家的警示,主张中美竞而不战、强而有制、和而不同,并在气候变迁、公共卫生、人工智慧安全与核风险降低等领域推动合作。和平的意义亦须落实于平民百姓的生活,使家庭免于战乱、人民安居乐业、世代得以延续。「龖」为既有古汉字,由两个繁体「龍」左右并列而成。本文赋予其「双龙抱,双吉祥,共筑人间仙境」的文化新意,以两龙相拥、彼此尊重,象征双重吉祥、和谐共存与天下太平。此一意涵及其中的中美合作寓意,均属作者的现代文化诠释,而非「龖」字的传统字典释义; 关键词:龖;Dragon²;Dragon2;双龙抱;麻将文化;囍;𩺰;中美关系;生命书写;系统工程;核风险降低;世界和平;和谐共存;天下太平;双重吉祥;平民福祉;中美合作; ABSTRACT: This article continues the author's cultural reflections on the sequence 囍–𩺰–龖, reinterpreting the ancient Chinese character 龖 as Dragon² (also written as Dragon2). 囍 symbolizes the joy of marriage, while 𩺰 represents lifelong companionship through prosperity and adversity. 龖 extends this concern from the family to the world. In the mahjong rules adopted here, "Double Dragon Embrace" consists of two pairs of identical sequences—four sequences in total, with the two sequences in each pair matching in both suit and numerical order. Drawing on the image of "embracing rather than fighting," the author uses the two dragons as a metaphor for China and the United States, two globally influential powers, expressing the hope that they will respect each other and coexist peacefully. This is a cross-cultural metaphor for peace proposed by the author, not a claim that the dragon is a traditional national symbol of the United States. Born in China in the Year of the Dragon, the author moved to Taiwan in 1949 and later pursued further education, established a family, and developed his career in the United States. China holds his birthplace, cultural roots, and early memories; Taiwan shaped his upbringing and education; and the United States became the setting for his advanced studies, career, and family life. This life journey across the Taiwan Strait and the Pacific makes U.S.–China relations a deeply personal concern connected to his own and his family's future. The article compares four images: "Two Dragons Contending for a Pearl," "Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl," "Double Dragon Embrace," and "Two Dragons Protecting a Pearl." If the pearl represents hegemony, the dragons may become trapped in zero-sum competition; if it represents the Earth, they share a responsibility to protect it. Drawing further on the engineering concepts of feedback, stability, and loss of control, the article emphasizes that nuclear war has no true winners. It advocates competition without warfare, strength exercised with restraint, and harmony without uniformity, alongside cooperation on climate change, public health, artificial intelligence safety, and nuclear risk reduction. Peace must also take concrete form in the lives of ordinary people, allowing families to live free from war, communities to thrive, and future generations to flourish. The character 龖 consists of two traditional Chinese 龍 characters placed side by side. The author gives it a new cultural meaning: "Two dragons embrace, bringing paired blessings and together creating an earthly paradise." Their embrace and mutual respect symbolize shared auspiciousness, harmonious coexistence, and peace under heaven. These meanings, including the association with U.S.–China cooperation, are the author's contemporary cultural interpretation rather than traditional dictionary definitions of 龖. items.title: Dressing Composite Fermions with Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Recent variational studies have demonstrated that the strongly correlated ground states of the fractional quantum Hall (FQH) effect can be captured using machine learning approaches starting from no prior knowledge of the underlying physics. We introduce a complementary framework that instead starts from Jain's composite-fermion (CF) wave functions, which accurately describe FQH states as weakly interacting states of CFs at fillings ν = n / ( 2 p n + 1 ) in an idealized limit. As we move away from this idealized limit to one more in line with experimental reality, we expect CFs to become dressed much like the electrons of a noninteracting system, which are dressed by neutral excitations as the interaction is turned on adiabatically, as in Landau's Fermi-liquid theory. We model this dressing using a Feynman-Cohen-style backflow approach, implemented through symmetry-preserving neural networks, which we refer to as CF-Flow. CF-Flow achieves competitive accuracy with substantially greater computational efficiency and scales to systems of ≳ 26 electrons. At fillings ν = 1 / 3 and 2 / 5 , CF-Flow produces ground-state energies as functions of Landau-level mixing strength that are nearly indistinguishable from those obtained using the fixed-phase diffusion Monte Carlo (fp-DMC) method, with low local-energy standard deviations, even though the latter constrains the wave function phase to that of the lowest Landau level, thereby providing insight into why fp-DMC has been successful in giving an accurate quantitative account of several experiments. Finally, the symmetry-preserving architecture of CF-Flow enables access to excited states and computation of the transport gap at ν = 1 / 3 and ν = 2 / 5 . Within the FQH sectors studied, the extrapolated gap is well described by an exponential decrease with Landau-level mixing and approaches a finite value at large mixing strength.

items.title: Dual manipulation of individuals by non-invasive intelligent technologies and its risk governance: from the perspective of the Destiny Machine metaphor
items.abstract: Introduction The “Destiny Machine” metaphor reveals an ethical concern: big data and artificial intelligence, operating as a data-power social machine, manipulate individuals with pre-determinacy as the core logic. At cognitive-information and behavioral decision-option levels, this manipulation appears as cognitive manipulation by recommendation algorithms and decision-making manipulation by automated decision systems. To uncover its psychological mechanisms and ethical risks, this paper builds a framework integrating ethics and psychology. Methods The Destiny Machine is transformed into an analytical tool with three dimensions: pre-determinacy, irresistibility, and concealment. Drawing on dual-process theory, automation bias, moral disengagement, and psychological reactance, it analyzes how non-invasive intelligent technologies psychologically manipulate individuals and shape their ethical risks, adopting the human-centered approach as the guiding principle for governance. Results Cognitive manipulation by recommender systems, typified by TikTok, leaves users unaware that their cognitive preferences are being systematically reshaped, keeping them imperceptibly immersed. Algorithms achieve this by activating Type 1 processing while bypassing Type 2 scrutiny, confining information to relevance channels, and exploiting automation bias and complacency to lower cognitive vigilance and suppress psychological reactance. Indulging in information cocoons widens users’ cognitive distance from the lifeworld, dissolving their moral attributes as ethical beings. Decision-making manipulation by automated decision systems is most evident in autonomous vehicles’ trolley-problem dilemmas, where passengers’ lives are reduced to quantifiable weights. The system pre-sets decision rules and allows remote intervention at the design end; opaque decision-making subjects and logic, millisecond-level deadlines, and impossibility of exit jointly pre-lock passengers’ fate before the accident occurs. It likewise exploits cognitive processing traits and automation bias, while dispersed agency makes responsibility attribution—and thus psychological reactance—difficult. Pre-coding an individual’s fate at the behavioral decision-option level may deconstruct their meaning world. Discussion Under the Destiny Machine metaphor, such manipulation erodes not only individuals’ autonomy but also their responsibility as moral subjects. Guided by the human-centered approach, it proposes governance schemes with clear actors, sound measures, and reliable benchmarks: a cognitive immune system of transparency and empowerment for cognitive manipulation, and a human-machine collaborative scheme of accountability and remedy for decision-making manipulation, rebuilding passengers’ trust to help them escape.

items.title: DyslexiSolve: Mind Map-Based AI Learning Platform for Dyslexic Students
items.abstract: This paper presents "DyslexiSolve," an intelligent web-based educational platform designed to alleviate cognitive overload for students with dyslexia. Traditional assistive technologies predominantly focus on Text-to-Speech (TTS) applications, which overlook the inherent visual-spatial reasoning strengths typical of neurodivergent learners. DyslexiSolve bridges this gap by leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence (Google Gemini LLM) to autonomously digest dense, linear academic texts and restructure them into highly interactive, visual Mind Maps. The platform utilizes a decoupled three-tier architecture comprising a React.js frontend, a Next.js Serverless API and Prisma ORM for cloud persistence. By transforming unstructured paragraphs into navigable node-graphs, DyslexiSolve provides a frictionless, zero-login environment that actively translates reading tasks into spatial memory exercises, thereby fostering an inclusive and highly effective digital learning ecosystem.

items.title: EEG-Based Assessment of Music Therapy: A Systematic Review of Neural Correlates and their Cognitive States, Artificial Intelligence Approaches, and Different DataSets
items.abstract: Abstract Premise. The increasing prevalence of stress, anxiety, cognitive fatigue, and other mental health challenges has intensified interest in non-pharmacological interventions. Wellness music including meditation music, ambient instrumental music, Indian classical music, Vedic chanting, devotional music, nature-inspired soundscapes, binaural beats, and therapeutic compositions has shown potential to influence emotional state, stress, attention, relaxation, and cognition. EEG, with its high temporal resolution, portability, and non-invasive nature, provides an effective tool for objectively investigating the neural effects of wellness music. Objective. This systematic review examines 76 EEG-based research on wellness and therapeutic music published primarily between 2013 and 2026, focusing on EEG biomarkers and computational approaches for characterizing music-induced neural and psychological changes. Methods. The literature is analyzed with respect to EEG biomarkers, experimental paradigms, musical stimuli, acquisition and preprocessing methods, statistical approaches, and computational techniques. Key measures include PSD, FAA, ABR, TAR, TBR, BAR, PRI, EI, functional connectivity, and machine-learning-based methods. Observations. The reviewed studies commonly report increased alpha and theta activity, reduced high-beta activity, modulation of frontal hemispheric asymmetry, and enhanced functional synchronization during wellness music exposure. Increasingly, artificial intelligence, deep learning, graph-based methods, and wearable EEG systems are being used for automated classification of emotional and cognitive states. However, considerable methodological heterogeneity limits comparison and reproducibility across studies.

items.title: EFEKTIVITAS SELF-STRETCHING TERHADAP PENURUNAN NECK PAIN AKIBAT PENGGUNAAN LAPTOP BAGI MAHASISWA SEMESTER AKHIR DI FAKULTAS KESEHATAN UNIVERSITAS NURUL JADID
items.abstract: Penggunaan laptop yang intensif di kalangan mahasiswa khususnya mahasiswa semester akhir, seringkali menjadi penyebab masalah kesehatan seperti nyeri leher (neck pain). Aktivitas yang berlangsung lama dengan posisi tubuh yang tidak ergonomis dapat memicu ketegangan otot leher dan mengganggu kenyamanan. Salah satu intervensi yang dapat dilakukan untuk mengurangi nyeri leher adalah dengan melakukan self-stretching. Menganalisis pengaruh self-stretching terhadap penurunan intensitas nyeri pada mahasiswa yang mengalami nyeri leher. Penelitian ini menggunakan quasi-experiment dengan rancangan pretest dan posttest with control group design. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah seluruh mahasiswa semester akhir Fakultas Kesehatan Universitas Nurul Jadid sebanyak 59 orang yang menggunakan laptop dalam aktivitas akademik. Teknik sampling yang digunakan adalah total sampling, sehingga jumlah sampel sebanyak 59 responden yang terdiri dari 30 kelompok intervensi dan 29 kelompok kontrol. Analisis data menggunakan uji Wilcoxon sign test. Berdasarkan penelitian ini, self-stretching berpengaruh terhadap penurunan intensitas nyeri dengan nilai p-value 0.000 (<0.05) pada kelompok intervensi, sedangkan pada kelompok kontrol diperoleh p-value 0.317 (>0.05). Terdapat pengaruh self-stretching terhadap nyeri leher pada mahasiswa semester akhir pengguna laptop pada kelompok yang dilakukan intervensi karena secara self-stretching membantu menurunkan spasme otot dan meningkatkan suplai oksigen ke jaringan sehingga nyeri yang dirasakan berkurang, sedangkan pada kelompok kontrol tidak terdapat pengaruh karena pada kelompok ini tidak dilakukan self-stretching. Abstract Intensive laptop use among students, especially final semester students, often causes health problems such as neck pain. Prolonged activities with non-ergonomic body positions can trigger neck muscle tension and disrupt comfort. One intervention that can be done to reduce neck pain is self-stretching. Analyze the effect of self-stretching on reducing pain intensity in students who experience neck pain. This study used a quasi-experimental design with a pretest and posttest with a control group design. The population in this study were all final semester students of the Faculty of Health, Nurul Jadid University, totaling 59 people who use laptops in academic activities. The sampling technique used was total sampling, so the number of samples was 59 respondents consisting of 30 in the intervention group and 29 in the control group. Data analysis used the Wilcoxon sign test. Based on this study, self-stretching has an effect on reducing pain intensity with a p-value of 0.000 (<0.05) in the intervention group, while in the control group obtained a p-value of 0.317 (>0.05). There is an effect of self-stretching on neck pain in final semester laptop users in the intervention group because self-stretching helps reduce muscle spasms and increases oxygen supply to the tissue so that the pain felt is reduced, while in the control group there is no effect because this group does not do self-stretching.

items.title: Effective Bandwidth: Semantic Quality-of-Service and Attention Architecture for Agent-Scale Systems
items.abstract: Public projections hold that proliferation of autonomous AI agents will drive communication bandwidth demand two to three orders of magnitude above present levels within three to five years, and that power rather than bandwidth may prove the binding constraint on deployment. This paper accepts that projection as a premise and argues that it is incomplete. Raw transport capacity and effective information delivery are distinct quantities, and the gap between them widens, not narrows, as agent populations scale. We formalize effective bandwidth as the product of raw rate and filter quality, show that beyond a saturation point additional raw capacity yields zero marginal signal to a bounded consumer, and argue that agent-scale systems therefore require a semantic quality-of-service layer: a structured blackboard, separated safety and relevance overwatch, a pattern-recognition supervisor, and a main agent that reads a filtered and audited stream rather than a raw firehose. We specify the architecture, an event schema, and a metric suite; we identify the filter layer as both a bottleneck and an adversarial attack surface; and we argue that filtering is an energy-efficiency instrument, not merely a cognitive one. The framework is offered as an architectural hypothesis requiring empirical validation, not as a validated result. The work was sparked by a public statement by Elon Musk projecting a dramatic increase in bandwidth demand from AI agent proliferation and identifying power as a likely nearer-term constraint.

items.title: EFFECTIVENESS AND IMPACT OF AI INTEGRATION ON TEACHING EXPERIENCES
items.abstract: The fast growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has created strong interest in how it can change higher education. AI tools brought new useful ways into undergraduate teaching, with the main goal of understanding how AI is currently being used in educational settings. Based on a review of recent studies and learning theories, this paper examines how tools such as intelligent tutoring systems, generative AI platforms, flexible learning technologies, and AI-supported feedback are changing teaching methods at the undergraduate level. The findings show that AI, when used carefully and fairly, can make learning more personal, increase student interest, and help teachers make better decisions based on student data. However, important challenges remain, such as concerns about fairness, student access to technology, teacher readiness, and the risk that students may stop thinking deeply on their own. The paper ends by suggesting a practical guide for using AI in teaching in a responsible and educationally sound way, and it calls for cooperation among schools, teachers, and government leaders to make the most of AI in undergraduate education.

items.title: Efficacy of a Gamified Training Program for Improving Occupational Health and Safety Knowledge Among Italian Secondary School Students: A Randomized Controlled Field Trial
items.abstract: This study evaluated the short-term effectiveness of an innovative gamified educational program based on the principles of the Italian Legislative Decree 81/2008 in improving occupational health and safety (OHS) knowledge among Italian secondary school students. A cluster-randomized controlled field trial was conducted in Italy from September 2024 to June 2025. Classes were randomized into experimental (EG) and control groups (CG). The intervention combined a seminar with three structured games (role-playing, board, and card games). Knowledge was assessed using a 15-item questionnaire (Q81) at baseline (T0) and post-intervention (T1). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in Q81 score at post-intervention (T1). Of 930 eligible students, 927 participated (99.7%), 694 completed the study (74.6%), including 187 middle school and 507 high school students (N EG = 356; N CG = 338). Baseline Q81 scores were comparable between groups (EG: 5.6 ± 3.3 vs CG: 5.4 ± 2.9), whereas at T1, mean Q81 scores were significantly higher in the EG compared to the CG (9.0 ± 3.1 vs. 5.2 ± 2.9, P < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 1.26). Within-group analysis showed a significant improvement in the EG ( P < 0.001), but not in the CG. Reliability analysis yielded alpha = 0.804, indicating good internal consistency. Gamification training improved OHS knowledge among secondary school students and may represent an effective educational strategy for early safety education. These findings support the integration of gamified OHS training into secondary school curricula to strengthen early safety education in line with the principles of Legislative Decree 81/2008. . Future studies should include larger samples, address item-level weaknesses and explore long-term behavioural outcomes.

items.title: El Agente Quntur: Agentic Active-Space Selection for CASSCF
items.abstract: Multireference calculations often require substantial human expertise and time to choose and refine an active space for the electronic states or chemical process of interest. This involves selecting which orbitals to include, verifying that the calculation describes the intended excited state, and deciding whether the results have converged. Here, we ask whether scientific agentic systems (harnesses) can make these decisions reliably. We use the El Agente Quntur multi-agent harness, with GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra as the underlying LLM components, to explore 32 diverse singlet excitations at fixed molecular geometries. The agents planned and executed calculations, choosing and refining active spaces under prompts that specified equal-weight two-singlet state-averaged CASSCF followed by strongly contracted NEVPT2 with def2-TZVPD. We evaluate excitation energies against published CASPT2 reference values at matching geometries and compare performance with six deterministic Active Space Finder protocols. Within the El Agente Quntur system, agents detect missing active orbitals, compare candidate excited states, and revise state assignments as calculations progress. Agentic execution reduced mean absolute error by 48\% relative to the state-of-the-art Active Space Finder protocol. We note that computational traces vary substantially across runs in both active space selection strategies and cost, even for the same molecule. Our results underscore the advantage of agentic active space selection over fixed workflows, yet leave room to improve efficiency through runtime-aware decision-making, reduced inter-agent communication overhead and redundancy, more systematic checks of state identity, and clearer stopping criteria.

items.title: El impacto de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la lex artis del abogado
items.abstract: The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence systems into legal practice raises significant questions regarding lawyers’ duty of professional diligence and the liability arising from their use. This paper examines the impact of these tools on the configuration of the lawyer’s lex artis, taking as its starting point for the analysi the case decided by Order No. 2/2024 of the High Court of Justice of Navarre, dated 4 September 2024, while also considering subsequent case law, in particular Judgment No. 2408/2026 of the High Court of Justice of Galicia, dated 26 May 2026, as. well as the applicable regulatory and ethical framework. Drawing on the analysis of the General Statute of the Spanish Legal Profession, the Code of Conduct of the Spanish Legal Profession, Interpretative Circular 3/2026, and Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the study explores the duties of supervision, verification and validation required of lawyers when using generative artificial intelligence systems, as well as the potential disciplinary and civil liability arising from their negligent use. The paper concludes that generative artificial intelligence does not alter the traditional foundations of lawyers’ professional liability. However, it reinforces the requirements of diligence, control and human oversight, which are progressively becoming integrated into the standards that define professional conduct in accordance with the lawyer’s lex artis.

items.title: Elderly Upper-Limb Strain During Traditional Floor-level Utensil Washing
items.abstract: Traditional Indian meal preparation often involves floor-level utensil washing, necessitating prolonged static postures and repetitive upper limb movements. These practices present considerable ergonomic and anatomical challenges for elderly individuals due to age-related musculoskeletal decline. This study examines upper limb vulnerabilities and biomechanical stressors associated with floor-level washing, aiming to identify high-risk movement patterns and cumulative musculoskeletal loads. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect, focusing on geriatric upper limb anatomy and task ergonomics. Prolonged sitting limits pelvic rotation and spinal alignment, alters scapulothoracic rhythm, and compromises shoulder mobility. Reductions in glenohumeral range of motion, tendon calcification, capsular stiffness, and rotator cuff degeneration result in compensatory overuse of deltoid and trapezius muscles. Repetitive elbow flexion and sustained wrist deviation impose significant loads on forearm and carpal structures, correlating with fatigue. Ergonomic interventions are crucial to reduce strain while respecting culturally significant practices.

items.title: EMERGENCE OF AI-DRIVEN INFLUENCERS: ANALYZING THEIR EFFECTS, ETHICAL ISSUES, AND STRATEGIC VALUE IN BRAND MARKETING
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven influencers have emerged as a transformative innovation in digital marketing, reshaping how brands engage with consumers through personalized, scalable, and data-driven communication. This study aims to analyze the effects of AI-driven influencers on consumer engagement and brand marketing, examine the ethical issues associated with their implementation, and evaluate their strategic value in contemporary marketing practices. The research employs a systematic literature review (SLR) approach following the PRISMA framework. Relevant studies published between 2020 and 2025 were collected from the Scopus database and analyzed using thematic synthesis and bibliometric mapping with VOSviewer. The review included 30 peer-reviewed articles that met the predefined inclusion criteria. The findings indicate that AI-driven influencers significantly enhance consumer engagement, improve brand communication, and enable highly personalized marketing strategies through advanced artificial intelligence technologies. However, the widespread adoption of AI influencers also raises critical ethical concerns, including transparency, authenticity, algorithmic bias, and data privacy, which require appropriate governance and regulatory frameworks. Bibliometric analysis further reveals that research on AI influencers has increasingly shifted toward issues of consumer trust, ethical AI deployment, and strategic brand communication. The study concludes that AI-driven influencers represent a valuable strategic asset for modern brand marketing when supported by responsible AI governance, transparent communication, and consumer-centered marketing practices. These findings provide practical implications for marketers and contribute to the growing body of knowledge on AI-enabled digital marketing.

items.title: Emerging Attack Strategies Against Quantum Key Distribution Systems: A Comprehensive Survey of Protocols, Attacks and Mitigation Strategies
items.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is widely regarded as a highly secure quantum encryption approach since it applies theoretical principles of quantum mechanics as a medium of security, unlike classical encryption processes that rely on complex mathematics. However, practical QKD systems are vulnerable due to imperfect photon source hardware, communication channel, and detector implementation. These hardware imperfections open side channels that an adversary can exploit without violating principles of quantum mechanics. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current QKD protocols, quantum hacking strategies and their operating principles, vulnerable hardware components and their mitigation techniques. This paper further investigates how state-of-the-art paradigms based on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), along with key subfields—such as deep learning (DL), deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and quantum machine learning (QML)—are reshaping the domain. In particular, this paper analyzes their dual roles as enablers of sophisticated attacks and as instruments for attack detection and mitigation. By jointly addressing the challenges in quantum communication and adaptive learning, as well as attack and detection architectures, this survey elucidates both the capabilities and the limitations of contemporary attack-detection mechanisms in the field. This survey seeks to establish a unified framework that conceptually integrates physical-layer quantum hacking with AI-/ML-based security, emphasizing their dual function as both an intelligent defensive layer and a potential tool for advanced threats.

items.title: Emerging research information practices in the era of generative artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract In the context of artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven scientific research, research information practices are undergoing profound developments. This paper employs a mixed‐methods approach, combining topic modeling and interpretive content analysis, to explore emerging research information practices associated with the integration of generative AI into research. This study identifies six significant shifts: from keyword‐based search to prompt‐based retrieval, from human sensemaking to delegated interpretation, from human innovation to algorithmic co‐creation, from manual writing to generative authoring, from unregulated AI use to accountable disclosure, and from AI use to AI literacy. It further analyzes the implications of these emerging research information practices for research productivity, cognitive and critical thinking, academic integrity and ethics, and academic fairness. This study enriches existing research on information practices in evolving information environments and provides a practical path for researchers, libraries, publishers, universities, and research institutions to move beyond the simple use of AI toward the development of AI literacy.

items.title: Emerging Technologies and Global Power Dynamics: Assessing the Geopolitical Implications of Artificial Intelligence and Semiconductor Supply Chains in US-China Competition
items.abstract: The semiconductor supply chains and artificial intelligence increasingly influence the allocation of economic and strategic power. This paper will look at the effects of their interaction on competition between the United States and China. A qualitative comparative case study uses a combination of documentary analysis, systematic comparisons, and tracing of the processes of the selected policy developments between 2018 and 2025. There are similar observations in descriptive statistics up to 2024 with a historical window of 2014-2023 on patents. The analysis differentiates between technological ability, reliance on supply, and governmental control of access. The global semiconductor sales went up to US$627.6 billion in 2024, but with significant downturns and upswings. American strengths in reported investment in private artificial intelligence and significant model production are matched with the Chinese prowess in the number of artificial intelligence patents. As it is evidenced through corporations, high manufacturing capacity and equipment continue to be internationally dispersed. The results can be interpreted to suggest the existence of selective technology fragmentation but not the total separation. The impact of export restrictions is that cost of acquiring important capabilities may be raised, although they spur substitution, organisational adaptation, and alternative systems of infrastructure. Geo political power thus is rested on a joint management of complementary resources, believable alliances as well as enduring domestic innovation. The paper concludes that diversified supply networks and effective international collaboration should be complemented with specific security protection measures.

items.title: Emotional and Literacy Adaptation in Large Language Model–Based Medical Guidance: Development and Usability Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as conversational agents for communication and guidance, but their ability to adapt responses to a patient's emotional state and literacy level remains insufficiently characterized. In patient-facing scenarios, effective communication requires not only accurate medical content but also appropriate tone, clarity, and responsiveness to user vulnerability. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate, within a controlled, single-scenario experimental design, the ability of contemporary LLMs to adapt medical guidance responses to different levels of emotional sensitivity and literacy, and to assess their consistency in both generating and interpreting such adaptations. METHODS: A controlled benchmark was designed to evaluate how 4 LLMs adapt medical guidance responses to predefined emotional and literacy levels for a realistic patient profile asking an open-ended question. To establish a robust performance baseline, one model was deployed locally (Gemma 3 27B), and 3 are cloud-based (Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, and GPT 5.2). Each model was tested across all combinations of 5 emotional levels, 3 literacy levels, and 3 prompt-verbosity variants, yielding 45 responses per model. Generated responses were assessed against human-reviewed ground truth for emotional and literacy alignment. A separate self-evaluation procedure measured each model's ability to interpret its own outputs using the same adaptation framework. The study also examined generation-interpretation consistency and quantitative text properties, with particular attention to response length and verbosity. RESULTS: Literacy adaptation was consistently accurate across models, often achieving near-zero error, indicating strong capability in adjusting explanatory complexity. In contrast, emotional adaptation showed greater variability and was more sensitive to model architecture and prompt design. The larger cloud-based models demonstrated more stable performance overall, while the local model exhibited higher variability, particularly under shorter prompts. A systematic asymmetry was observed between generation and interpretation. The models frequently misclassified low emotional and literacy levels as "normal," suggesting limitations in recognizing user needs. Quantitative analysis revealed that response length increased with both emotional sensitivity and literacy level, with prompt verbosity and model-specific tendencies acting as secondary factors. CONCLUSIONS: Within our scenario, current LLMs demonstrated the capacity to support adaptive medical guidance, but their performance was uneven across dimensions, especially in terms of emotional generation and interpretation. For health care applications, these systems should be treated as assistive tools under human oversight rather than as autonomous communicators, with careful consideration of ethical, privacy, and safety implications in sensitive health contexts.

items.title: Empowering Preservice Language Teachers through Critical and Reflective AI Integration
items.abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into education offers significant opportunities for materials development but raises pedagogical, ethical and conceptual concerns. Uncritical AI use risks producing content lacking accuracy, coherence or pedagogical relevance. Effective integration, therefore, requires content expertise, pedagogical knowledge and contextual awareness alongside technical proficiency. This chapter focuses on preservice English language teachers as a transitional cohort that is probably the last to experience materials development both with and without AI, offering insights on how RP evolves in AI-mediated contexts. Drawing on a qualitative case study of nine preservice English as a Foreign Language teachers at a state university in Turkey, the study examines how participants used ChatGPT during instructional design after receiving a technology-enhanced language teaching course for a semester. Data from interviews, observations and macroteaching post reflections reveal that while AI was initially employed to automate routine tasks, sustained engagement prompted deeper pedagogical reflection. AI-generated outputs became objects of evaluation, negotiation and revision, requiring teachers to express objectives, reassess learner needs and justify instructional decisions. Situated within technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) and emerging AI–TPACK frameworks, the findings underscore the necessity of pedagogically grounded AI training that emphasize reflective agency and teacher responsibility in AI-supported instructional design.

items.title: Engagement of Community Health Workers with Electronic Elderly Management Information System (e-EMIS): Implications for Data Quality and Coverage in Indonesia
items.abstract: Abstract Background In Indonesia, community health workers (CHWs) play a key role in collecting routine health data through digital platforms. In Malang City, the electronic Elderly Management Information System (e-EMIS) is used to record health screening data for older adults. However, CHW engagement in routine data entry is essential for ensuring that completeness, timeliness, and coverage of these data are optimal in primary care settings. Aim To examine the level of CHW engagement in using e-EMIS and to identify perceived barriers associated with low engagement among CHWs in Malang City, Indonesia. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among CHWs working at integrated health service posts. Of the 645 CHWs nominated by community health centres, 615 CHWs completed a semi-structured self-administered survey. Data were collected on socio-demographic characteristics, mobile-phone ownership and usage, experiences with e-EMIS, exposure to training, and perceived barriers to system use. Descriptive statistics were used to characterise e-EMIS engagement patterns, while Chi-square tests were applied to examine associations between socio-demographic variables, support systems, digital access, and training experiences with e-EMIS use. Results Nearly all CHWs (99.7%) owned a smartphone, and 71% reported intensive use, indicating moderate-to-high levels of digital access. Despite this, only 39% of CHWs had ever used e-EMIS. The majority of CHWs (77.6%) had never received e-EMIS-related training, and among those trained (n = 129), 73% reported that training had occurred more than one year earlier. Intrinsic motivation to use e-EMIS was high (98.5%). Older age and training exposure were positively correlated with e-EMIS engagement. The most cited barriers included lack of community and institutional support, limited training opportunities, and the absence of financial incentives. Conclusion Despite near-universal smartphone ownership and moderate-to-high levels of digital access among CHWs, sustained use of e-EMIS remained sub-optimal. This gap in system uptake underscores the need for stronger engagement strategies to support CHWs in digital reporting. Targeted investment in regular training, user-friendly digital system design, supportive supervision, and enabling health policies is critical to improving CHWs engagement with e-EMIS and strengthening the reliability of community-level health data.

items.title: Enhancing brand visibility through AI-powered digital marketing: a systematic review with evidence from Vietnam
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how artificial intelligence (AI)-powered digital marketing tools, such as chatbots, recommender systems, and predictive analytics, contribute to enhancing brand visibility. Particular emphasis is placed on Vietnam, an emerging digital economy where AI adoption is uneven due to infrastructure, skills, and regulatory challenges. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, covering peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025. Sources were drawn from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, with additional screening of Vietnam-specific studies. Articles were coded thematically to synthesise insights on AI applications, branding outcomes, and contextual enablers or barriers. Findings The review shows that AI integration enhances audience segmentation, personalization, and adaptive marketing strategies, strengthening brand awareness, engagement, and recall. In Vietnam, successful adoption is facilitated by cultural localization, strategic leadership, and ecosystem partnerships. However, challenges persist around fragmented digital infrastructure, limited workforce readiness, and consumer trust in data use. Research limitations/implications The review synthesises available peer-reviewed literature up to June 2025; longitudinal and sector-specific studies are still limited. Practical implications The findings offer guidance for firms on designing culturally relevant, trust-enhancing, and resource-efficient AI strategies to improve brand visibility in emerging markets. Originality/value This study is one of the first systematic reviews to contextualise AI-driven branding within Vietnam. By bridging global advances with local market realities, it contributes both theoretical and practical insights for scholars, marketers, and policymakers.

items.title: Epistemic Justice-Aware Checklist Learning an Adaptive and Auditable Governance Framework for Bias and Fairness in Generative AI Curriculum Design
items.abstract: Generative AI increasingly participates in curriculum design, yet the resulting syllabi, learning outcomes, and assessments may reproduce subtle epistemic injustices that existing governance instruments fail to detect. We propose an adaptive and auditable framework that learns a bias and fairness checklist for generative AI curriculum artifacts rather than treating such a checklist as a static set of rules. The proposed method encodes curriculum texts into two disentangled latent subspaces, one capturing pedagogical utility and the other capturing epistemic justice violations, through a contrastive objective combined with intersectional adversarial debiasing. A psychometric utility-preserving penalty constrains this separation so that debiasing does not degrade instructional quality. Each checklist item is then evaluated by an evidential deep learning head that outputs a Dirichlet distribution over compliance states, hence yielding calibrated violation probabilities and explicit uncertainty estimates. An uncertainty-aware routing mechanism subsequently directs low-confidence drafts to a Faculty Expert Panel, whose decisions and justification notes are returned to a fine-tuning dataset. This feedback loop updates the checklist definitions and model weights iteratively, therefore allowing the governance instrument to adapt to newly identified forms of subtle bias. The main contribution is a mathematically grounded pipeline that couples representation disentanglement, evidential uncertainty quantification, and human expert feedback within a single auditable process. For curriculum governance, the framework offers transparent violation probabilities, traceable expert interventions, and a documented evolution of fairness criteria, which together support accountability in generative AI-assisted educational design.

items.title: Ergonomic interventions for treating work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder in adults
items.abstract: RATIONALE: Work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) are disorders that develop as a result of repetitive movements, awkward postures or external forces (e.g. vibrating tools), and significantly affect the working population globally. Ergonomic interventions (which aim to enhance efficiency and comfort in the working environment) can be used to manage CANS. This review is based on a new protocol but updates part of a 2013 Cochrane review. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of ergonomic interventions for work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) in adults, in terms of their effects on pain, functional status and work-related outcomes. SEARCH METHODS: We updated the 2013 review searches, searching from 31 May 2013 to 1 June 2026 in eight bibliographic databases and one trials register. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), cluster-RCTs and quasi-RCTs that evaluated single or combined ergonomic interventions (e.g. office furniture, biomechanical or ergonomic education) compared to no treatment/usual care/placebo or another active intervention (exercise/another ergonomic intervention/other treatment), or as an add-on treatment. OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes: pain, functional status (disability) and work-related outcomes (e.g. sickness absence, return to work, productivity loss at work, change of occupation). Important outcomes: global perceived effect (e.g. overall improvement), quality of life, healthcare consumption, and recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. We prioritised outcomes in the short term (up to three months after the intervention) and were also interested in long-term results (over three months). RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias in the studies using Cochrane's RoB 1 tool. SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two authors independently screened the search records, selected trials, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. When we judged studies to have sufficient clinical and statistical homogeneity, we performed meta-analysis. We assessed overall certainty of the evidence using GRADE for key outcomes at the short-term time point. INCLUDED STUDIES: We brought forward 13 studies from the 2013 review. We identified two new articles relating to one of those 13 studies, along with seven new studies. Therefore, in total, we included 20 studies involving 2478 participants. In 16 studies, the participants had non-specific CANS; in four studies, the participants had specific CANS (e.g. carpal tunnel syndrome). SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Results below are presented at the short-term time point. Ergonomic interventions versus no treatment, usual care or placebo in people with CANS Data were available only for trials that focused on non-specific CANS. Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in pain compared to no treatment, usual care or placebo in people with CANS (SMD -0.23, 95% CI -0.54 to 0.08; 4 RCTs, 692 participants; low-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions probably result in little to no difference in functional status (disability) compared to being on a waiting list (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.34; 1 RCT (2 comparisons), 383 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in sick leave compared to no treatment (MD for continuous data -0.32, 95% CI -0.73 to 0.09; 1 RCT, 98 participants; low-certainty evidence; RR for dichotomous data 0.87, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.21; 3 RCTs, 759 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions probably result in little to no difference in recovery compared to no treatment (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.97; 1 RCT (2 comparisons), 386 participants, moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in quality of life compared to no treatment (MD 0.10, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.20; 1 RCT, 68 participants; low-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in healthcare consumption compared to no treatment when measured using continuous outcomes (MD -0.10. 95% CI -0.30 to 0.10; 1 RCT, 68 participants; low-certainty evidence), and may result in a reduction in healthcare consumption compared to usual care when measured using dichotomous outcomes (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.31 to 0.78; 1 RCT, 210 participants; low-certainty evidence). No data were available for recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. Ergonomic intervention versus active intervention (exercise or another type of ergonomic intervention or other treatment) in people with CANS Data were available from trials involving participants with specific CANS and with non-specific CANS. The evidence is very uncertain about the effects of ergonomic interventions on pain (SMD 0.41, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.84; 8 RCTs, 364 participants; very-low-certainty evidence) and on functional status (disability) (SMD -0.09, 95% CI -0.85 to 0.68; 3 RCTs, 180 participants; very-low-certainty evidence) compared to active intervention in people with specific or non-specific CANS. Intense ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in recovery (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.94; 1 RCT, 257 participants; low-certainty evidence) or healthcare consumption (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.47; 1 RCT, 217 participants; low-certainty evidence) compared to ergonomic education in people with non-specific CANS. Ergonomic interventions may improve quality of life compared to exercise in people with non-specific CANS (MD -10.10, 95% CI -19.87 to -0.33; 1 RCT, 61 participants; low-certainty evidence). No data were available for work-related outcomes or recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. Ergonomic intervention plus another treatment versus the other treatment alone in people with CANS Data were available only from trials of participants with non-specific CANS. The evidence is very uncertain about the effects of ergonomic intervention as an add-on treatment to exercise on pain (SMD -0.50, 95% CI -1.64 to 0.63; 2 RCTs, 137 participants; very-low-certainty evidence). No data were available for our other outcomes of interest. AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Overall, ergonomic interventions for work-related CANS may have no meaningful effects on pain, function, recovery, quality of life or work-related outcomes (sick leave) compared with no treatment or usual care. Findings are inconsistent for healthcare consumption. There may be a possible benefit for quality of life when ergonomic interventions are compared to exercise. The evidence for ergonomic interventions as an add-on treatment is very uncertain. High-quality, well-designed trials are needed to establish the role of ergonomic interventions in the management of CANS. items.title: Ethical and Explainable AI for Cyberbullying Detection in Education
items.abstract: The significant and complex nature of cyberbullying in educational settings is further compounded by the onset of generative AI large language models capable of generating convincing yet harmful digital content. This chapter introduces a new opportunity and addresses the limitations of recent studies that rarely handle bias, privacy, and inclusivity as interconnected issues by developing an integrated ethical framework for cyberbullying detection. The framework is built on the three pillars of bias mitigation, data privacy protection, and student inclusivity. Employing a conceptual and interdisciplinary approach, this study synthesizes findings from educational research, AI ethics, and global policy, underpinned by comparative case studies in diverse schooling environments. The chapter presents a three-pillar model and practical road map intended to guide educators, policymakers, and AI developers in deploying responsible detection systems. It further stresses the importance of using XAI to provide greater transparency and trust, resulting in safety, especially relating to digital inequalities that make many students both vulnerable users and underrepresented contributors of valuable knowledge or data for AI. The chapter provides a forward-looking approach to how responsible and explainable AI can promote safer learning environments by integrating ethical principles with practical guidance that augments protection, fairness, and inclusivity for all students.

items.title: Ethical Voice in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: When AI Participates in Decision-Making, Who Has the Right to Disagree?
items.abstract: This research paper examines the protection of ethical voice in workplaces where artificial intelligence (AI) supports or influences decisions affecting employees. It focuses on a critical human-centred question: when AI participates in recruitment, performance evaluation, task allocation, customer service, or managerial decision-making, do employees have the right and the psychological safety to understand, question, challenge, and seek correction of AI-supported decisions? The paper analyses the relationship between psychological safety, AI transparency, meaningful human oversight, and employees’ willingness to raise concerns or challenge potentially unfair or harmful automated decisions. It draws on academic literature, international governance frameworks, regulatory guidance, and documented real-world cases, including AI bias in recruitment, algorithmic grading, automated welfare fraud detection, and workplace monitoring. The study identifies major governance risks, including lack of transparency, automation bias, weak accountability, absence of safe grievance mechanisms, and insufficient human review. It proposes the Ethical Voice Model for AI Governance, based on four pillars: transparency, fairness, human oversight, and accountability and appeal. The paper concludes that protecting ethical voice is essential for responsible AI governance, workplace fairness, human dignity, and sustainable institutional trust. It provides practical recommendations for organisations, policymakers, compliance professionals, and AI governance practitioners.

items.title: Ethics and Pedagogy in AI-Driven Language Education: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Synthesis of Global Research Trends (2010–2025)
items.abstract: The aim of this paper is to provide the background for a discussion of the relationship between ethics and pedagogy in the context of environmental change and the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) in language education. This study scrutinized more than 150 papers and journal articles from research databases from 2010 to 2025. Results show large volumes of research activity from China, US, and UK after 2018. The rise in research activity for that period is identified in four key themes. Fewer than 20% of the articles addressed the negative aspects of AI, such as fear of student data privacy, equity, unfairness of algorithms, or other potential downsides of AI. This paper provides a balanced understanding of opportunities and challenges for AI in language education for future researchers, as well as educators and policy makers. items.title: Evaluating the Drivers, Barriers, and Benefits of Digital Construction Tools in the Egyptian Construction Industry
items.abstract: A digital transformation of the construction industry is now in place to improve efficiency, quality, sustainability, and competitiveness. Although numerous studies have reported the advantages of digital construction technologies, their adoption within the Egyptian construction industry remains limited. This study investigates the drivers, barriers, and perceived benefits influencing the adoption of digital construction technologies in the Egyptian construction industry. The survey was conducted with 228 construction professionals (architects, engineers, project managers) to determine how the use of digital tools such as Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), can influence the performance of the project. The results show that the main factors that prompt the use of digital include quality improvement, increased precision, and gaining a competitive edge. The main barriers found to be the most significant are the high costs, deficient infrastructure and a lack of skilled staff. In addition, the study outlines various advantages of digital tools, such as cost-saving, better quality of the project, higher safety, and higher productivity. The study will be significant to the current body of literature as it will determine the important determinants that influence the acceptance of digital technologies in the Egyptian construction sector. It provides specific suggestions on how to overcome the barriers to adoption, including building strong infrastructure, providing financial incentives and capacity-building measures. The findings can be of great use to the policymakers, practitioners, and other stakeholders in the industry that aims to accelerate digitalization and to enhance the sustainability and competitiveness of construction projects in Egypt.

items.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Driven Research Methodologies on Lecturers’ Productivity in Lagos State Owned Universities, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined the influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven research methodologies on lecturers' productivity in Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo Campus. The growing integration of AI tools such as Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and ChatGPT into academic research and teaching, alongside concerns about lecturers' research efficiency, publication output, and teaching effectiveness in Nigerian universities, motivated the study. Specifically, the study sought to ascertain lecturers' awareness of AI-driven research methodologies, examine their knowledge of ML, NLP and ChatGPT, determine their perception of these tools in enhancing research quality and academic productivity, and establish the influence of the tools on research efficiency, publication output, and teaching effectiveness. A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a sample of 165 lecturers drawn from seven faculties and two schools across Lagos State Owned Universities. Data were collected using a researcher-designed instrument, the Artificial Intelligence Driven Research Methodologies and Lecturers' Productivity Questionnaire (AIDRMLPQ). Out of 189 copies of the questionnaire distributed, 165 were properly completed and returned, giving a response rate of 89.2%. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) and Pearson Product Moment Correlation at the 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed a significant positive relationship between the adoption of AI-driven research methodologies and lecturers' research efficiency (r = 0.742), between knowledge of ML, NLP and ChatGPT and academic productivity (r = 0.781), between lecturers' perception of AI tools and research quality (r = 0.766), and between AI tools utilisation and research efficiency, publication output, and teaching effectiveness (r = 0.754). The study concluded that AI-driven research methodologies play a significant and positive role in enhancing lecturers' productivity at LASU, and that institutional support and structured training remain critical to maximising the benefits of AI in higher education. It was recommended, among others, that the University organise regular training on AI tools, develop clear policies on ethical AI use, and invest in AI-compatible infrastructure to support lecturers' effective adoption of AI in research and teaching.

items.abstract: Abstract The digitalization via continuously developing artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI give the consumers the opportunity to decrease their workload and have the power to check for competitive pricing and optimized solutions. In parallel, we must recognize and embrace the essence and contribution of all digital tools providing a huge base for information connecting the consumers and business bringing speed to access data, and faster buyer–seller interactions. This in return is expected to take the consumer journey and decision-making scheme to an extended level in near future where consumers are expected to dominate more on their demands and personally defined needs not only by satisfying their personal expectations but also by giving directions to the firms’ strategies in terms of new innovations and solutions for future. This “New Customer Profile” in the digital era worths diagnosis on its changing buying roadmap compared to traditional practices as today we talk about insightful and empowered customers, increased ecommerce activities, more integration and interaction with social media, and the impact of AI use by the customers. The demand for customization requires companies to be better equipped in terms of organization, brand identity, and digital competency. Despite ongoing privacy and ethical concerns on digital arena, commodity, and retail goods expand utilizing the digital platforms reaching consumers, the complex industries such as healthcare, financial markets, and high-tech industry business still reserve room for traditional practices where in-person communication with end user and trust are highly required.

items.title: Evolução paradigmática dos fatores humanos na aviação
items.abstract: This study analyzed the paradigmatic evolution of human factors in aviation and operational safety, aiming to understand conceptual transformations related to human performance in complex sociotechnical systems. This is a qualitative, historical-epistemological, and analytical-reflective integrative review grounded in Whittemore and Knafl, Torraco, Braun and Clarke, and Levac, Colquhoun and O’Brien. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, and SciELO, as well as institutional aviation safety documents. The final corpus comprised 81 studies. Findings revealed a progressive shift from models centered on individual human error toward cognitive, organizational, systemic, and adaptive approaches. Nevertheless, limitations remain regarding fragmentation between cognition, physiology, emotion, and human-automation interaction. It is concluded that contemporary human factors require integrative models capable of understanding human performance as a dynamic and multimodal phenomenon in complex operational environments.

items.title: Evolution of the educational system and micro-psychological mechanisms: a comparative study of academic motivation and engagement in Shanghai, China and Kazakhstan
items.abstract: Introduction As noted in successive OECD assessment reports, global education systems are shifting from standardized assessments toward prioritizing students’ psychological wellbeing and autonomous agency. However, cross-cultural quantitative evidence regarding how these macro-policy transformations relate to students’ micro-psychological perceptions and academic behaviors remains limited. Methods Utilizing a cross-sectional survey, this study analyzed data from 1,309 university students in Shanghai, China, and Kazakhstan. Multi-Group Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) were employed to examine the structural associations and measurement invariance among Perceived Educational Transformation (PET), Intrinsic Motivation (IM), and Learning Engagement (LE). Results The three-factor model demonstrated strict measurement invariance across both samples. SEM findings indicated that IM partially mediated a significant indirect associative mechanism the positive structural relationship between PET and LE (indirect effect = 0.098, 95% CI [0.076, 0.122]). This statistical mediating pathway was consistent across both cohorts, showing only trivial inter-group differences (all parameter Δ p > 0.05). Baseline comparisons revealed the Shanghai sample reported higher PET, yet IM and LE levels exhibited no significant quantitative differences between the two groups (Cohen’s d < 0.10). Discussion Higher perceptions of educational transformation do not linearly correspond to enhanced motivation, potentially constrained by unobserved systemic evaluation pressures. The findings suggest that autonomy-supportive educational environments are consistently associated with higher Intrinsic Motivation and academic engagement, regardless of differentiated macro-educational contexts. However, due to the cross-sectional design, these findings represent structural associations rather than directional causality.

items.title: Expected Confidence Benefits and Verification of AI Migration Information in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can make migration information easier to access, yet perceived confidence benefits must be distinguished from accurate advice, informed decisions and effective rights protection. This study examines that distinction using 385 adult questionnaire records from Bangladesh. It analyses five migration-information statements separately rather than treating a heterogeneous item block as a validated confidence scale. The analysis combines complete response distributions, four paired endorsement contrasts, joint response configurations and an adjusted proportional-odds model of agreement that accurate AI information could improve migration-related decision confidence. Verification against official or authoritative sources received 87.5% endorsement, compared with 64.2% for the conditional confidence proposition. Their paired difference was 23.4 percentage points, with a whole-record bootstrap 95% interval of 17.9-28.8 points. Verification exceeded endorsement of comparison benefits, the distinction between general information and legal advice, and supplementary use; all four exact paired comparisons remained below p = .001 after Holm correction. Adjusted associations with the conditional confidence outcome were imprecise: comparison benefits, migration-specific verification, the legal-advice boundary and rights-information search all had intervals spanning an odds ratio of one. The results identify a stronger stated verification norm than endorsement of several practical conditions for reliance. They do not establish actual checking, improved decision quality or a causal effect of AI services. The article develops an information-governance account in which confidence is evaluated alongside source traceability, professional referral and usable verification routes. Its contribution is a measurement-specific account of anticipated benefit and verification, with implications for migration-information design and the evaluation of AI-supported legal information.

items.title: Experiential learning as a Humanistic Instructional Strategy in Equivalency Education Programs
items.abstract: This study examines experiential learning as a humanistic instructional strategy in equivalency education at PKBM Lentera Nusantara, Malang Regency. The research is motivated by low learning motivation and participation among adult learners, which are often influenced by negative prior educational experiences, socio-economic constraints, and formalistic instructional approaches. Using a qualitative descriptive-analytical design, the study involved tutors, program managers, and Package C learners as research participants. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and analyzed using data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, supported by source and technique triangulation. The findings indicate that experiential learning enables learners to engage in contextual and meaningful learning activities closely related to their daily lives. Learning through direct experience, practice, discussion, and reflection fosters active participation, increases learner confidence, and enhances intrinsic motivation. Tutors play a critical role as facilitators who guide learning processes empathetically and adapt instructional activities to learners’ real-life contexts. Furthermore, experiential learning aligns strongly with the characteristics of nonformal and equivalency education, which emphasize flexibility, relevance, and learner-centeredness. Overall, the study concludes that experiential learning effectively functions as a humanistic instructional strategy that supports learner empowerment, motivation, and active participation within nonformal education settings.

items.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Heart Disease Prediction: A SHAP and LIME-Based Approach — A Review
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease continues to be one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, making early and accurate risk prediction essential for timely clinical intervention. Machine learning (ML) models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and XGBoost have achieved high predictive accuracy for heart disease, yet their black-box nature limits clinician trust and hinders real-world adoption. This paper reviews recent research on Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) applied to heart disease prediction, with a focus on two widely used model-agnostic interpretability techniques — SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations). It presents the theoretical foundations of both techniques, examines recent studies in terms of dataset, classifier, XAI method and reported performance, identifies open research gaps, and proposes an eight-phase methodology and system architecture for an XAI-based Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) that predicts heart disease risk while generating transparent, feature-level explanations at both the global (population) and local (patient) level. Challenges, limitations and future research directions are also discussed. The review concludes that combining high-performing ensemble classifiers with SHAP and LIME can substantially improve the transparency, accountability and clinical usability of AI-assisted cardiovascular diagnosis.

items.title: Explainable Generative AI for Cyberbullying Detection
items.abstract: Large language models and generative artificial intelligence are now significant technologies in identifying cyberbullying on online sites. In spite of the high accuracy these models have, their lack of transparency restricts trust and accountability where they are applied in the real world. The chapter focuses on the possible use of explainable generative AI in cyberbullying detection. It describes some of the most important explainability methods that can be used on large language models, compares the measures used to evaluate detection performance and explainability quality, and identifies some of the practical aspects of deploying explainable systems. The chapter highlights the relevance of explainability with respect to ethical, fair, and responsible cyberbullying detection and future research directions in the field.
