items.abstract: This review paper examines the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in sports injury prediction and athlete performance management. It reviews existing approaches for assessing injury risk using athlete health indicators, training load, sleep, fatigue, stress, and previous injury history. The paper discusses the potential of machine learning methods, including Random Forest, to support injury-risk classification and data-driven athlete monitoring. It also considers challenges related to data quality, model reliability, interpretability, and the responsible use of predictive systems in sports and healthcare. The review identifies research gaps and highlights opportunities for developing integrated athlete-monitoring systems that support injury prevention and performance management. The findings are intended to inform future research and the development of responsible AI-based sports health applications.

items.title: Explainable multi-agent AI systems for intelligent software engineering and business automation
items.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) are revolutionizing software programming and enterprise business automation in the 4th industrial revolution era. Current multi-agent systems, however, are constrained in being able to collaborate, in understanding how to reach consensus, in their knowledge sharing and in their ability to adapt to changes and therefore are not suitable for certain industrial critical applications. To address the above challenges, this paper introduces a cognitive swarm-based multi-agent framework with collaborative reasoning, collective cognitive memory, explainable decision intelligence, digital twin simulation and autonomous governance, which are integrated into an explainable cognitive swarm control framework XCognitive SwarmNet. Proposed framework mathematically models agent collaboration, trust, explainability, Knowledge sharing and Optimization of the flow of business tasks to support the complete Software Development Lifecycle and Intelligent Business process Automation. By using the powerful and representative software engineering and business process datasets, some experimental assessments are performed and the proposed mechanism is compared to six state-of-the-art multi-agent approaches. The proposed framework completes the task with 98.1% accuracy, gains in 22.8% in the software quality, achieves 97.5% in explainability fidelity, optimizes the workflow by 95.9% and optimizes the efficiency of agent collaboration by 94.7% with a 27.4% reduction in execution time. Overall, the results showed that XCognitive SwarmNet is a suitable solution to achieve transparent, adaptive and trustworthy AI-driven digital transformation for Industry 4.0.

items.title: Exploring AI Literacy Through a Semester-Long Course
items.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has raised questions about students' understanding of responsible use and academic integrity. This descriptive study examines students' experiences in a semester-long AI literacy course in a humanities program at a large public university in the United States. The course addressed AI history, capabilities and limitations, academic integrity, and ethical considerations, and provided structured opportunities to explore multiple tools. Pre-course (N = 31) and post-course (N = 25) surveys examined tool familiarity, reported use, perceived usefulness, awareness of limitations, and self-reported understanding of AI-related academic integrity. At the end of the course, respondents described more task-specific tool selection, greater attention to evaluating outputs, and increased confidence in identifying appropriate uses of AI. These findings reflect perceptions and reported practices rather than independently assessed AI literacy or ethical competence. Because the instruments differed, respondents were not individually matched, and no comparison group was included, the findings cannot establish causal improvement. The study discusses implications for AI literacy instruction in humanities and language education and for future assessment of students' AI-related knowledge and practices.

items.title: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly explored as collaborative learning partners in mathematics education, yet it remains unclear what makes an AI recognizable as a peer. This study examines how domain experts perceive and interact with an adaptive LLM-based peer agent combining a Big Five-informed persona with motivational state modulation for collaborative mathematics problem solving. Through thematic analysis of expert interviews, we identify conditions shaping peer perceptions, including emotional safety, shared control, and collaborative reasoning. Participants primarily judged the AI through its social behavior rather than mathematical capabilities. The AI was perceived more as a peer when it created a non-judgmental space, engaged in tentative reasoning, displayed appropriate imperfection, and respected participants' pace. Conversely, blind agreement and over-instruction reduced trust and shifted perceptions toward a tutor role. Based on these findings, we propose human-centered design dimensions for AI peer agents to guide future peer-oriented learning systems.

items.title: Exploring Art Appreciation Across Three Virtual Museum Configurations: Do Experience Patterns Differ by Formal Art Education?
items.abstract: This exploratory study examines how art appreciation varies across three virtual museum configurations, particularly the White Cube, Traditional Museum, and Contextualized Configurations, and whether participants’ experiential patterns differ according to their formal art education. Using a mixed-methods approach, this study integrates quantitative findings across six dimensions of aesthetic experiences with qualitative insights into the perception of composition, color, and detail. Examining the role of participants’ formal art education provides insights into how individuals with different educational backgrounds draw on perceptual, spatial, and interpretive cues. Based on these findings, the study identifies two complementary areas of design implications to support virtual art appreciation: configuration-level design considerations and participant-informed design opportunities, encompassing perpetual scaffolding, interpretive layering, analytical exploration, environmental context, and flexible flow. These implications suggest potential strategies for offering more inclusive virtual museum experiences that could accommodate different educational backgrounds and engagement preferences.

items.title: Exploring Copyright Protection for Artificial Intelligence Outputs Based on the Interaction Between Technology and Law
items.abstract: In response to the issues of whether artificial intelligence (AI) outputs can be protected by copyright, to whom the rights should belong, and how infringement should be determined, this study adopts a method combining normative analysis and historical analysis. Starting from the historical logic of copyright law’s response to technological change, it sorts out and analyzes institutional responses under the impact of printing, photography, audio and video recording, and Internet technologies, and identifies three patterns: human beings as the creative subject, a balance between empowerment and limitation of rights, and judicial action taking the lead. The study shows that generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) has the attribute of a tool, and the copyrightability of its outputs depends on the substantial intellectual control exercised by humans in prompts, parameters, selection, and revision. The degree of human contribution should be used as the standard for distinguishing weak protection from strong protection; fair use should be moderately relaxed at the training input end, substantial similarity should be strictly regulated at the output end, the burden of proof on developers should be strengthened, and judicial adjudication should comprehensively consider the responsibilities of all parties.

items.title: Federated Learning and Blockchain for Privacy-Preserving Cyberbullying Detection
items.abstract: The proliferation of generative AI has transformed cyberbullying, enabling large-scale automated harassment while creating detection opportunities. This chapter introduces a privacy-preserving framework combining federated learning and blockchain for collaborative cyberbullying detection across educational institutions without centralizing student data. Our approach addresses three critical challenges: maintaining student privacy under GDPR and FERPA regulations, ensuring transparent and accountable AI decision-making through explainable AI techniques, and establishing trust among participating institutions through blockchain-based model provenance verification. We validate our framework through experiments on combined datasets from multiple educational platforms, demonstrating 91.8 percent detection accuracy for LLM-generated harassment while maintaining differential privacy guarantees (ε=1.0). The blockchain layer successfully prevents 96.3 percent of model poisoning attacks in federated training scenarios, while SHAP-based explanations achieve 87 percent alignment with expert-annotated harassment indicators. Our work demonstrates that privacy, accountability, and effectiveness need not be competing objectives in educational AI systems, offering a practical blueprint for multi-stakeholder collaboration in combating GenAI-amplified cyberbullying.

items.title: Federated learning in cancer imaging: a comprehensive review and future outlook
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has promoted the advancement of data-driven AI medical models, bringing transformative changes to the field of traditional cancer imaging by significantly improving diagnostic accuracy. However, despite these remarkable achievements, a fundamental challenge remains: data privacy. The sensitive nature of medical data and stringent privacy regulations often limit data sharing and collaboration between institutions, hindering the development of robust and generalizable AI models. Federated learning has emerged as a promising solution to address this challenge. By enabling multiple institutions to collaboratively train artificial intelligence models without sharing their local datasets, federated learning reduces the privacy leakage risks associated with conventional centralized AI training while utilizing the collective power of diverse medical data. From 2019 to 2026, extensive research has explored the applications of federated learning in cancer imaging, demonstrating its potential to advance the field while preserving patient confidentiality. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the progress in applying federated learning to cancer imaging, highlighting key studies and their contributions. We also discuss the unique challenges facing federated learning, such as data security, data heterogeneity, and communication overhead. Finally, we explore some potential future research directions. This review aims to provide insights into the evolving role of federated learning in cancer imaging.

items.title: Field Study: Expected Change in Technology, Organizations, and Business in the Digital Era
items.abstract: Abstract In today’s continuously evolving globe, digital technologies are transforming firms, the way organizations act, think, and strategize to maintain a profitable and sustainable business. This requires the proactive strategy of companies with a digital mindset and culture, adapting to the new dynamics of the unbarriered markets. Customers are now more powerful with access to information, aware of their needs, with an increasing concern on a cleaner, accountable, ethical, and transparent future world. This chapter evaluates the answers of commercial business professionals from corporate world on qualifying the expected impacts of digitalization on organizations, in organizational structure, the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) integration, the influence of social media, the changes in consumer behavior, and how the new sales professionals are expected to manage the new customer journey in terms of the value creation, differentiation, and engagement for competitive advantages. A second survey conducted among industry stakeholders from various businesses assesses the required attributes of a sales professional in the digital era. The analysis of the results indicate the increasing transformation in digital era where most firms are urged for digitalization as the common mind of interviewees addressing mostly hybrid organizations benefiting from the human and digital power depending on the complexity of the industry. Digital competency of sales professionals in predicting market intelligence and insights for strategic decision-making, customer centricity, solution selling, engaging customers for co-value creation for innovation, and loyalty underline the new norms of sales professionals in the digital era.

items.title: FinSight: An Evidence-First Financial Analysis Chatbot with Explainable Query Intelligence
items.abstract: Financial question answering is difficult because user queries often combine ambiguous intent, entity aliases, temporal scope, market data, news narratives, and advice-seeking language. Fluent responses become risky when the resolved entity, selected data sources, and evidence gaps remain hidden. This paper presents FinSight, an evidence-first financial analysis chatbot for questions about China’s financial markets. The system separates evidence production from final-response generation. Its Query Intelligence backend converts a natural-language query into explicit natural-language understanding (NLU) and retrieval artifacts, including the normalized query, product type, intents, resolved entities, source plan, retrieved documents, structured records, evidence coverage, warnings, ranking traces, and analysis summary. Downstream modules provide frontend rendering, numerical analysis, document sentiment analysis, constrained LLM-based summarization, and follow-up-question prediction. In a local evaluation of 10,000 query-style cases, including 6,236 finance-domain and 3,764 out-of-scope queries in Chinese and English, FinSight achieved finance-domain recall of 0.975, out-of-scope rejection accuracy of 0.9729, intent micro-F1 of 0.9407, topic micro-F1 of 0.9208, and retrieval Recall@10 of 0.9664. In addition, all contract checks passed in a 32-case end-to-end fuzz matrix. Typed evidence handoffs allow readers to trace each generated claim to a retrieved item or explicit warning rather than treating the final response as unsupported output.

items.title: Fishing in the Archive
items.abstract: Abstract This essay considers the effects of the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) on research in the humanities—specifically in the field of the history of music theory—by linking these transformative developments to the momentous rise of relevance-ranked full-text search over the preceding quarter century. It considers both the extraordinary potential of LLM-assisted archival work and its risks, examining AI-enabled archival searches and new research paradigms on the one hand, and opaque mediation, “AI slop,” and above all the dangers of deskilling and cognitive surrender on the other. It argues that music theorists and humanists more broadly must actively engage with these tools rather than avoid them, since scholars trained in earlier research regimes are uniquely positioned to recognize what stands to be gained—and lost—as close reading gives way to new methods (and habits) of research.

items.title: Forecasting financial support for government institutions using artificial intelligence: The case study of museums
items.abstract: Subject. Forecasting the financial support of public institutions based on regional panel data of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To develop and test a methodology for forecasting the financial support of museums using artificial intelligence methods. Methods. A panel dataset of 85 constituent entities of the Russian Federation for 2018–2024 was compiled. Machine learning methods were applied, including gradient boosting, regularized linear models, and their ensembles. Hyperparameter tuning was carried out using an artificial intelligence agent (AI agent) based on the Qwen3.5‑27B language model. Thirty‑two computational experiments were conducted. Forecast accuracy was assessed using the median absolute percentage error (MdAPE); rolling validation was applied over four test years (2021–2024). Results. The gradient boosting model achieves an MdAPE of 8.1% across regions, outperforming the best naive forecast by 1.9 percentage points and the previous‑year forecast by 4.6 percentage points. The average MdAPE under rolling validation was 12%. For 64% of the regions, the forecast error does not exceed 15%. Infrastructure‑related characteristics of institutions (28.6%) and personnel‑related characteristics (22%) demonstrate the highest predictive power. A systematic tendency to underestimate forecasts for large regions was identified; this is driven by discretionary budgetary decisions that cannot be predicted based on operational indicators. Conclusions and Relevance. Artificial intelligence methods demonstrate an advantage over traditional econometric approaches in the context of nonlinear relationships and interregional heterogeneity. The proposed methodology is applicable to forecasting financial indicators of public institutions in other sectors, provided that similar operational data at the regional level are available. The results can be used by public authorities in budget expenditure planning and in preliminary assessments of expected levels of financial support.

items.title: Forecasting LLM‐Enabled Biorisk and the Efficacy of Safeguards
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Capabilities of large language models (LLMs) on several biological benchmarks have prompted not only excitement about their usefulness for research but also concern about biosecurity risks. We recruited 46 subject‐matter experts in biology and biosecurity, and 22 generalist forecasters to estimate the risks of growing LLM capabilities. Most respondents expected some hypothetical LLM capabilities to increase their estimates of risk and dramatically underestimated the rate of LLM progress in those capabilities. When these capabilities arose, the median forecast did update as anticipated. The median expert initially predicted a 0.3% annual risk of a human‐caused epidemic that causes 100,000 deaths. This estimate then rose to 1.5% conditional on several hypothetical LLM capabilities, including matching the performance of a top‐performing team of virologists on a virology troubleshooting test, which the median expert did not expect to occur until 2030. Given this finding, we conducted a baselining study and found that LLMs already crossed this performance threshold in April 2025. A follow‐up survey conducted after these results were available found that forecasters significantly updated their median unconditional risk estimates upward, with the new median expert forecast of annual risk rising to 1.5% (as anticipated by the earlier conditional forecasts). More encouragingly, most experts thought that the adoption of LLM safeguards and mandatory nucleic acid screening would negate the risk associated with some hypothetical LLM capabilities.
